source_metadata.exact_title: Pharmacokinetics of Intraperitoneal Cefalothin and Cefazolin in Patients Being Treated for Peritoneal Dialysis-Associated Peritonitis

atoms.canonical_statement: The study aimed to describe the pharmacokinetics of intraperitoneal cefalothin and cefazolin in patients treated for PD-associated peritonitis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The aim of this study was to describe the pharmacokinetics of IP cefalothin and cefazolin in patients treated for PD-peritonitis.

atoms.canonical_statement: Eligible participants were adults at least 18 years old with clinical PD-peritonitis who had been maintained on CAPD or APD for at least 1 month and were treated with intraperitoneal cephalosporin therapy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients were eligible if at least 18 years old and maintained on continuous ambulatory PD (CAPD) or automated PD (APD) for at least 1 month.

population.label: Eligible PD-peritonitis patients
inclusion_criteria: CAPD or APD for at least 1 month
Clinical PD-peritonitis treated with IP cephalosporin therapy

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients who had received intraperitoneal antibiotics in the preceding 2 weeks were excluded.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients who had received a course of IP antibiotics in the preceding 2 weeks were not eligible for the study.

population.label: Study candidates
exclusion_criteria: Course of intraperitoneal antibiotics in preceding 2 weeks

atoms.canonical_statement: Nineteen patients were included: 8 received cefalothin and 11 received cefazolin.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Nineteen patients were included in this study (cefalothin n = 8 and cefazolin n = 11).

population.label: Adults with PD-associated peritonitis enrolled in the pharmacokinetic study

atoms.canonical_statement: Cefalothin was administered intraperitoneally at 15 mg/kg once daily, with gentamicin, in a 6-hour antibiotic-containing dwell.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: 15 mg/kg of cefalothin or cefazolin ... and gentamicin ... in a 6-hour dwell

population.label: Cefalothin group

exposures.details: Prescribed with gentamicin during routine PD-peritonitis care

atoms.canonical_statement: Cefazolin was administered intraperitoneally at 15 mg/kg once daily, with gentamicin, in a 6-hour antibiotic-containing dwell.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: 15 mg/kg of cefalothin or cefazolin ... and gentamicin ... in a 6-hour dwell

population.label: Cefazolin group

exposures.details: Physician-selected first-generation cephalosporin; prescribed with gentamicin

atoms.canonical_statement: All patients received four 2-L peritoneal dialysis exchanges per day during the acute phase; APD patients were switched to CAPD on admission.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: On hospital admission, APD patients were switched to CAPD during the acute phase of peritonitis. All patients received 4 exchanges per day with dialysate volumes of 2 L per exchange.

atoms.canonical_statement: Serial plasma and peritoneal-dialysis effluent samples were collected during the first 24 hours after the initial antibiotic dose.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Serial plasma and PD effluent samples were collected over the first 24 hours of therapy.

atoms.canonical_statement: Cefazolin and cefalothin concentrations were quantified by validated UHPLC-MS/MS assays; depending on matrix, lower limits of quantitation were 0.1–1.0 mg/L for cefazolin and 0.2–1 mg/L for cefalothin.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Cefazolin and cefalothin were measured by UHPLC-MS/MS ... the lower limit of quantitation for cefazolin in plasma and PD effluent was 0.1 – 1.0 mg/L and cefalothin was 0.2 – 1 mg/L.

atoms.canonical_statement: Pharmacokinetic parameters were estimated with a noncompartmental approach; concentrations below the assay lower limit of quantification were treated as zero.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A noncompartmental pharmacokinetic approach was used to analyze the data ... Concentrations less than the lower limit of quantification were considered zero.

atoms.canonical_statement: Continuous variables were summarized as median and interquartile range and compared between antibiotics with the Mann–Whitney test; p<0.05 was considered statistically significant.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Continuous variables are expressed as median (interquartile range), and the statistical difference between antibiotics was determined using the Mann-Whitney test ... A p value of 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

atoms.canonical_statement: Median intraperitoneal bioavailability was 0.92 for cefalothin and 0.93 for cefazolin (p=0.98).

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that once-daily intraperitoneal cefalothin carries a risk of subtherapeutic plasma and PD-effluent concentrations and that more frequent dosing may be required.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: with once-daily IP dosing, in contrast to cefazolin, there is a risk of subtherapeutic plasma and PD effluent cefalothin concentrations, so more frequent dosing may be required.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that cefazolin may be preferred when a first-generation cephalosporin is administered once daily for PD-peritonitis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Therefore, cefazolin may be the preferred treatment when a first-generation cephalosporin is to be given once daily in the treatment of PD-peritonitis.

atoms.canonical_statement: The single-dose design did not determine the effects of repeated doses, including the risk of drug accumulation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This is a single-dose study following the initial dose, so the effects of repeated doses on cephalosporin concentrations, including the risk of accumulation, are not determined.

atoms.canonical_statement: The elimination phase was estimated using only two samples to reduce inconvenience to patients.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: to limit inconvenience to patients, the elimination phase was determined using only 2 samples.

atoms.canonical_statement: The small sample prevented reliable subanalyses of peritoneal membrane transporter status and residual renal function.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Some subanalyses could not be performed due to the small number of patients, for example the influence of peritoneal membrane transporter status and residual renal function

atoms.canonical_statement: The supplement states that total and unbound cefalothin and cefazolin assays used UHPLC-MS/MS with matrix-specific preparation and validation for linearity, LLOQ, matrix effects, precision, and accuracy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The methods were validated for linearity, LLOQ, matrix effects and intra-batch precision and accuracy.

atoms.canonical_statement: The supplement identifies continuous intraperitoneal cefalothin dosing (500 mg/L loading, then 125 mg/L in each exchange) as an alternative regimen, while stating that whether it achieves defined concentration targets remains unclear.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: An alternative is the ISPD continuous dosing regimen (500 mg/L loading dose, then 125 mg/L in each exchange) but whether this achieves defined concentration targets remains unclear.

atoms.canonical_statement: The supplement notes that residual renal function could contribute to subtherapeutic cephalosporin concentrations; the study did not show a statistically significant effect but could not exclude one.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: although this was not a statistically-significant issue in our study, an effect cannot be excluded.
